fluff.overview:
The Sarissa, named for the ancient Greek spear, was one of the first BattleMechs produced in the Free Worlds League. Designed sometime shortly after 2470 as a contemporary of the Icarus and Mackie, the MN1-K was conceived by Corean Enterprises as a stopgap militia 'Mech intended to fill out the ranks of member-state militias against the threat of Lyran and Capellan BattleMech forces. The design philosophy prioritized ease of manufacture, allowing the Sarissa to be assembled in civilian IndustrialMech facilities by technicians with no specialized BattleMech training.

Though production was discontinued well before the Star League era, the Sarissa was revived centuries later during the Jihad by the Principality of Regulus. The design remains a symbol of the Free Worlds League's earliest efforts to field a domestic BattleMech force.
fluff.capabilities:
The MN1-D Sarissa is a fifty-ton medium 'Mech built entirely with primitive technology. Its 240-rated primitive engine provides a top speed of roughly sixty-five kilometers per hour, adequate for garrison duty but unimpressive by modern standards. The 'Mech's primary armament is a binary laser cannon mounted in the right arm, giving the design surprisingly significant firepower for a primitive chassis. A medium laser in the left arm and a small laser in the center torso provide secondary firepower at varying ranges, while a center-mounted machine gun with a half-ton of ammunition addresses the anti-infantry role Regulus specifically requested for civil disorder suppression.

The Sarissa's greatest weakness is its primitive armor. While carrying a respectable ten tons of protection, the near-commercial-grade materials offer substantially less coverage than modern BattleMech armor of equivalent weight. Fourteen single heat sinks manage the considerable waste heat from the binary laser adequately, though sustained fire alongside the other energy weapons can strain the cooling system. The absence of jump jets further limits the design's tactical flexibility, reinforcing its role as a straightforward garrison platform.
fluff.history:
The Sarissa's origins trace back to the early Age of War, when the Free Worlds League scrambled to develop its own BattleMech force after acquiring 'Mech technology in 2462. Designed sometime after 2470, the MN1-K was a mechanically reliable and durable machine that drew heavily on a century of IndustrialMech construction experience. Armed with a simple but effective weapons loadout and mounting as much armor as the remaining weight budget allowed, the Sarissa was welcomed by both civilians and militias who had been trembling under the threat of hostile BattleMechs.

The original Sarissa enjoyed modest success among Marik member-state militias, proving an adequate design for the era that outpaced the common Mackie, though it was not particularly impressive otherwise. Production at Corean Enterprises' Stewart facility was eventually discontinued, likely during or before the Star League era as more capable designs rendered the primitive 'Mech obsolete. For centuries, the Sarissa existed only as a historical footnote.

The design's resurrection came during the Jihad, when the Principality of Regulus suffered continuous damage to its military and industrial infrastructure. In the early 3080s, Regulus contracted Corean Enterprises to resume production of the ancient design. With Corean's BattleMech facilities beleaguered under the weight of the Jihad, the company turned to General Motors for subcontracted assistance in converting a civilian IndustrialMech plant on Futuna to produce the primitive design.

The MN1-D had only a short production run before Corean retreated from the Futuna factory and refocused on civilian IndustrialMechs amid skyrocketing demand for reconstruction. The MN1-D had proven quite unpopular with Regulan militias, but the Principality of Regulus insisted on continued 'Mech production, even if it had to be an IndustrialMech. Corean incorporated lessons from the MN1-D into the MN2-A SecurityMech, built on a more practical IndustrialMech chassis. Under pressure from the Principality, Corean has been dutifully building and shipping Sarissas to Regulan planetary militias in quantity, while quietly providing guidance on further refit efforts to improve the design's lackluster protection.
fluff.deployment: The MN2-A is a fundamental redesign of the Sarissa, converting the primitive BattleMech into a SecurityMech built on an IndustrialMech chassis. Incorporating lessons learned from the MN1-D's troubled reception, the MN2-A modernized the engine and chassis while upgrading to industrial-grade armor, though it still fell short of true BattleMech protection. The tradeoff drew comparisons to the Panther from detractors. Freed tonnage from the modernized components allowed the addition of extra heat sinks to address criticisms of the earlier model's thermal management. The MN2-A has been shipped to Regulan planetary militias in quantity under pressure from the Principality of Regulus.
